title: TLS
description:
TLS for every protocol: verify-full with a CA file, pinning the certificate, require,
and HTTPS. Needs `make it-up` (its test certificates). See `:help dbdash-tls`.

query.sql: SELECT version AS tls, cipher, bits FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid()

show.title: PostgreSQL, tls=verify-full with ca=
show.description:
`tls=verify-full&ca=...`: the chain must lead to the given root and the host name must
match; the row shows the TLS version and cipher PostgreSQL reports for this session.

query.sql: SELECT ssl, version FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid()

show.title: PostgreSQL, tls=pin
show.description:
`tls=pin&fingerprint=sha256:...`: the server's certificate must have exactly this
fingerprint (a wrong one fails and names the right one).

query.sql: SHOW SESSION STATUS WHERE Variable_name IN ('Ssl_version', 'Ssl_cipher')

show.title: MySQL, tls=require
show.description:
`tls=require` encrypts without checking the certificate; MySQL reports the version and
cipher of the session.

show.title: Redis, tls=pin
show.description:
Redis over TLS on port 16380 with a pinned fingerprint (`rediss://` would verify by
default).

show.title: HTTPS (verify-full by default) with ca=
show.description: HTTPS verifies the certificate and host name by default; `ca=` adds the test root.
